source_meta._title: '/locate', explorer maps, and treasure maps can cause extreme TPS lag, even leading to a complete server freeze if structure generation is turned off

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.14.4 in singleplayer, using the integrated server and a newly created world with Generate Structures set to OFF and commands enabled. This version and setup are selected because the report provides a direct singleplayer reproduction for 1.14.4.
preconditions: Install and launch the unmodified Java Edition 1.14.4 client; do not use OptiFine, mods, plugins, or a third-party server.
Use a disposable new world. No particular world seed is specified by the report.

The computer must remain available long enough for the observation subsystem to monitor the game after the command is submitted; the duration and severity of the response may depend on system performance.
Do not use an existing world whose chunks or structures were generated under different settings.
Trigger the test only once. Repeated /locate commands are unnecessary and may create additional lag or cause a watchdog termination.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation that runs Java Edition 1.14.4, then start the game.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is visible and identifies the running version as Minecraft 1.14.4.

steps.action: Select the Singleplayer button from the main menu.
steps.success_cue: The Select World screen is open.

steps.action: Select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is visible.

steps.action: Optionally give the disposable test world a recognizable name. Leave the world seed unspecified and leave the game mode and world type at their defaults; the report does not require particular values for them.
steps.success_cue: The new-world configuration screen remains open and the test world can be identified by its name.

steps.action: Select More World Options... to expose the structure-generation and command-permission settings.
steps.success_cue: The additional world options are visible, including Generate Structures and Allow Cheats.

steps.action: Select the Generate Structures button until its displayed state is OFF. Do not turn it back on before creating the world.
steps.success_cue: The option visibly reads Generate Structures: OFF.

steps.action: Select the Allow Cheats button until its displayed state is ON. This is needed so the supplied /locate command can be executed from in-game chat.
steps.success_cue: The option visibly reads Allow Cheats: ON while Generate Structures still reads OFF.

steps.action: Select Create New World to generate and enter the world using the displayed settings.
steps.success_cue: The loading screen completes and the player appears in the newly created world.

steps.action: Do not run the command during initial world loading. Wait until nearby terrain has rendered, the loading overlay is gone, the HUD is visible, and ordinary movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player can look and move normally in the loaded world before the test command is entered.

steps.action: Press the Open Chat control, which is T by default, to open the in-game chat entry field.
steps.success_cue: A chat input field with a text cursor is visible at the bottom of the screen.

steps.action: Type the report's command exactly into in-game chat. Include the leading slash and preserve the structure argument shown in the report. Do not submit it yet.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field contains exactly /locate Village.

steps.action: Press Enter once to submit the command. Do not issue another command, pause the game, open a menu, or attempt to close the world after submission; immediately hand control to the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: The /locate Village command has just been submitted and no additional test action has been initiated.

stor.handoff_condition: The player is in a newly created Minecraft Java Edition 1.14.4 singleplayer world made with Generate Structures set to OFF, and /locate Village has just been submitted once through in-game chat. Begin observing integrated-server responsiveness immediately without performing further player actions.
uncertainties: The report does not provide a required world seed, spawn location, game mode, difficulty, render distance, or hardware specification.
The time between command submission and any performance effect is hardware-dependent; no fixed wait duration is supported by the report.

The issue includes other trigger paths involving explorer maps and treasure-map chests, but this plan intentionally uses the simpler deterministic /locate Village path explicitly documented for a structure-disabled 1.14.4 singleplayer world.
Although the issue lists many affected versions, Minecraft Java Edition 1.14.4 is recommended because the report contains a complete, explicit reproduction sequence for that version.

The report describes TPS lag and possible complete freezing; the setup does not require a dedicated server because its 1.14.4 reproduction explicitly uses singleplayer, whose world runs on an integrated server.

source_meta._title: Clicking with an item that is out of stock in the villager trading menu with sufficient payment will allow purchase of the item regardless

stor.environment: A fresh, disposable single-player world running Java Edition snapshot 23w07a. Use Creative mode with commands enabled only for deterministic setup, then switch to Survival mode before interacting with the villager. Use an unmodified client with standard mouse-based inventory controls.
preconditions: Install and launch snapshot 23w07a in a separate launcher installation or game directory so the test does not affect normal worlds.
Create a new disposable world rather than opening an existing world in this snapshot.
Commands/cheats must be enabled so the custom villager, payment items, and Survival mode can be established deterministically.
Do not use mods, datapacks, or resource packs that change villagers, trading, inventory screens, or item behavior.
The test uses wheat as the villager's sold item because the report indicates that the affected item should be stackable.
Keep at least one empty player-inventory slot available for the purchased wheat.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft: Java Edition using the exact snapshot installation 23w07a.
steps.success_cue: The title screen identifies the running version as 23w07a.

steps.action: Create a fresh single-player world. Set the game mode to Creative and ensure commands or cheats are enabled before creating the world. No particular seed or experimental feature is required.
steps.success_cue: The player has entered a new world in Creative mode and can use commands.

steps.action: Wait before continuing until nearby terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: Surrounding chunks are visible and the player can move without initial world-loading pauses.

steps.action: Press the Open Chat control, which is T by default.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open.

steps.action: In chat, enter the supplied command exactly, including the leading slash, and press Enter. This summons a farmer villager approximately two blocks away with one custom trade: one emerald for one wheat, with only one use in stock.
steps.success_cue: A farmer villager appears approximately two blocks from the player, and chat does not display a command syntax error.

steps.action: Press T again to open chat.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open.

steps.action: Give the player one full stack of emeralds by entering the command exactly, including the leading slash, and pressing Enter.
steps.success_cue: A stack of 64 emeralds is present in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Press T again to open chat.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open.

steps.action: Switch to Survival mode by entering the command exactly, including the leading slash, and pressing Enter.
steps.success_cue: The player is in Survival mode; the normal health and hunger HUD is visible.

steps.action: Face the summoned farmer villager and use the Interact control on it, which is right-click by default.
steps.success_cue: The villager trading menu is open and shows a single offer exchanging one emerald for one wheat.

steps.action: Identify the three trade slots above the player inventory. From left to right, they are the first payment slot, the optional second payment slot, and the third or result slot on the right side of the trade arrow. Also identify the corresponding offer row in the left sidebar. Do not click the offer row, because the full emerald stack should be placed manually.
steps.success_cue: The first payment slot and the rightmost third/result slot can be targeted without closing the menu.

steps.action: Left-click the stack of 64 emeralds in the player inventory or hotbar to attach the full stack to the mouse cursor.
steps.success_cue: The emerald stack icon follows the mouse cursor.

steps.action: Move the cursor to the first, leftmost payment slot and left-click once to place the full emerald stack into that slot.
steps.success_cue: The first payment slot contains the emerald stack, and one wheat appears in the third/result slot.

steps.action: Perform exactly one ordinary trade by left-clicking the wheat in the third/result slot once. Do not Shift-click and do not repeat the click.
steps.exact_input: Left-click the wheat in the third/result slot once
steps.success_cue: One wheat is attached to the cursor, one emerald has been consumed, and the remaining emeralds are still available as payment.

steps.action: Move the cursor to an empty slot in the player inventory and left-click once to place the purchased wheat there.
steps.success_cue: The wheat occupies an inventory slot and the mouse cursor is empty.

steps.action: Wait for the trading menu to update after the one-use trade is exhausted.
steps.success_cue: A red X is displayed over the arrow for the wheat offer in the left sidebar, and the third/result slot is empty.

steps.action: Confirm that sufficient payment remains in the first payment slot. The expected setup leaves 63 emeralds there. If the emeralds were returned to the player inventory, manually move at least one emerald back into the first payment slot without closing the trading menu.
steps.success_cue: At least one emerald is present in the first payment slot while the offer still displays its red out-of-stock X and the third/result slot remains empty.

steps.action: Left-click the wheat that was placed in the player inventory to pick it up with the mouse. Release the mouse button after the click; do not use Shift-click or right-click.
steps.exact_input: Left-click the wheat in the player inventory
steps.success_cue: The wheat icon follows the cursor and its former inventory slot is empty.

steps.action: Move the cursor carrying the wheat over the empty third/result slot. Do not press a mouse button while moving the cursor.
steps.success_cue: The cursor is carrying wheat and is positioned directly over the empty third/result slot; sufficient emerald payment remains in the first slot and the offer remains marked with a red X.

steps.action: While still carrying the wheat on the cursor, left-click the empty third/result slot exactly once. Do not perform any additional inventory action after this click.
steps.exact_input: Left-click the empty third/result slot once
steps.success_cue: The specified trigger click has been issued while the cursor carried wheat, the out-of-stock offer was selected, and sufficient payment was present.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just left-clicked the empty third/result slot while carrying wheat on the cursor, with at least one emerald in the first payment slot and the trade row marked out of stock by a red X. Keep the trading menu open and hand control immediately to the observation subsystem.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, coordinates, or whether multiplayer is required. A fresh single-player world with Creative setup followed by Survival trading is a practical deterministic choice.
The custom one-use emerald-for-wheat villager is not supplied by the report. It is a deterministic setup replacement for finding, leveling, and exhausting a naturally generated villager trade.

The reporter states that the issue worked on stackable items to their knowledge but does not establish whether non-stackable items are unaffected. This plan therefore uses stackable wheat and does not test the non-stackable case.

The wording 'drag it over' is interpreted as picking the wheat up with one left-click, releasing the mouse button, moving the carried stack over the result slot, and then performing the separate left-click described by the report.
The attached video was not available in the supplied report contents, so no additional timing or cursor-motion requirements could be extracted from it.

source_meta._title: Villagers can sell experimental enchantments without the 1.21 experiment enabled

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft: Java Edition 1.20.5 Release Candidate 1 (launcher version name: 1.20.5-rc1)
stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition in a disposable single-player Creative world. Use the official launcher with snapshots enabled, no mods, no third-party datapacks, no resource packs that rename items, and all built-in experiments disabled. A Superflat world and frozen daytime are used as practical controls to make repeated villager profession changes easier; they are not stated requirements of the report.
preconditions: Install and launch exactly Minecraft: Java Edition 1.20.5 Release Candidate 1, not 1.20.5 Release Candidate 2 or the final 1.20.5 release.
Use a newly created test world rather than an important existing world because release-candidate versions can damage or convert worlds.
Leave both the Update 1.21 experiment and the Villager Trade Rebalance experiment disabled. Do not enable any other experiment or install an experimental datapack.
Use Creative mode with commands allowed so the villager, lectern, enclosure, and controlled daytime can be established without unrelated resource gathering.
Do not complete any trade with the test villager. Completing even one trade locks that villager's profession and offers, preventing the lectern-breaking reroll procedure.
The relevant mace-only enchantment names in this version are Density, Breach, and Wind Burst. Any displayed enchantment level is sufficient for identifying a matching offer.
Trade generation is random, so an unspecified number of rerolls may be required.

steps.action: Open the Minecraft Launcher. In Installations, enable historical snapshot installations, create or select an installation for 1.20.5 Release Candidate 1, and start it. If the launcher offers a separate game directory, use one dedicated to this test.
steps.exact_input: Installations -> Snapshots: enabled -> New Installation -> Version: 1.20.5-rc1 -> Play
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu loads and identifies the running version as 1.20.5 Release Candidate 1 or 1.20.5-rc1.

steps.action: From the main menu, open the single-player world list and begin creating a new world.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Set the world to Creative mode and turn Allow Commands or Allow Cheats on if it is presented as a separate option.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; Allow Commands/Allow Cheats: ON
steps.success_cue: The creation screen shows Creative mode, with commands permitted.

steps.action: Open the world settings and select the default Superflat world type. This avoids having to locate a clear construction area and reduces the chance of unrelated village workstations being nearby.
steps.success_cue: The selected world type is Superflat.

steps.action: Open the Experiments screen. Confirm that Update 1.21 and Villager Trade Rebalance are both off. Do not activate any experiment before returning to the creation screen.
steps.exact_input: Experiments -> Update 1.21: OFF; Villager Trade Rebalance: OFF
steps.success_cue: No experiment is selected and the world-creation screen does not show an experimental-world warning caused by enabling an experiment.

steps.action: Create the world and wait until terrain is rendered and normal player movement responds.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the new world, nearby terrain is visible, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Press F3 to open the debug overlay and verify the displayed client version is 1.20.5-rc1. Close the overlay with F3 after checking.
steps.success_cue: The debug overlay identifies 1.20.5-rc1, and the overlay is then closed.

steps.action: Verify the world's enabled datapacks. Press T to open chat, enter the command exactly with its leading slash, and press Enter. Inspect the resulting enabled-pack list for any Update 1.21 or Villager Trade Rebalance pack.
steps.success_cue: The enabled-pack output does not list an Update 1.21 experimental pack or a Villager Trade Rebalance experimental pack.

steps.action: Place the world at the beginning of villager working time. Open chat with T, execute the command exactly, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms the time was changed, and the world is in daylight.

steps.action: Freeze the daylight cycle so the villager remains in a suitable daytime schedule while trades are repeatedly rerolled. Open chat with T, execute the command exactly, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms that doDaylightCycle is now false, and the sun no longer advances.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Use its search field to obtain a Villager Spawn Egg, a Lectern, and enough full solid blocks for a small enclosure. Move all three item types into hotbar slots, then close the inventory with E or Esc. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen; select a slot using the number keys 1 through 9 or the mouse wheel.
steps.exact_input: E; search for "Villager Spawn Egg", "Lectern", and a full solid block
steps.success_cue: A Villager Spawn Egg, a Lectern, and enclosure blocks are present in accessible hotbar slots.

steps.action: On the flat ground, build an enclosure with an interior at least 3 blocks by 3 blocks and walls 2 blocks high. Leave the top open so the Creative-mode player can fly in and out. Do not place any lectern or other villager workstation yet.
steps.exact_input: Select the solid blocks and right-click to place them
steps.success_cue: A villager cannot walk out of the enclosure, and there is clear floor space inside for both one villager and one lectern.

steps.action: Select the Villager Spawn Egg in the hotbar. Aim at the floor inside the empty enclosure and use the egg once with right-click. Do not use the egg directly on an existing villager.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the enclosure floor once with Villager Spawn Egg selected
steps.success_cue: One adult, unemployed villager is standing inside the enclosure and cannot escape.

steps.action: Select the Lectern in the hotbar. Enter or hover over the enclosure in Creative flight, then right-click an empty floor block immediately beside the villager to place the lectern where the villager can walk up to it.
steps.exact_input: Right-click an empty floor block with Lectern selected
steps.success_cue: The lectern is placed inside the enclosure within direct walking distance of the villager.

steps.action: Wait without opening the trade screen until the villager claims the lectern and changes into a librarian. Continue only after the profession change is visible; green particles may also appear during the claim.
steps.success_cue: The adult villager is wearing the librarian profession outfit while the lectern remains accessible.

steps.action: With an empty hand or any non-interfering item selected, aim at the librarian and use right-click to open its trading interface.
steps.success_cue: The Trading screen is open and displays the novice librarian's current trade rows.

steps.action: Inspect every currently visible novice trade without completing one. For any trade whose output is an Enchanted Book, move the pointer over the output book icon and leave it there long enough for the tooltip to appear. Read the enchantment name and level. A matching target is a tooltip named Density, Breach, or Wind Burst at any level. Do not click the trade row's execution area, supply payment items, or take an output item.
steps.exact_input: Hover the pointer over each Enchanted Book output icon
steps.success_cue: The tooltip for the current Enchanted Book offer is visible and its enchantment name can be read, while no trade has been completed.

steps.action: If none of the current offers is an Enchanted Book with Density, Breach, or Wind Burst, press Esc to close the Trading screen. If one of those names is displayed, do not close the screen; stop the reproduction sequence at step 17 and hand control to the observation subsystem.
steps.exact_input: Esc only when no target mace enchantment is present
steps.success_cue: For a non-matching roll, the player is back in the world facing the same librarian and lectern. For a matching roll, the Trading screen remains open with the pointer over the target book output.

steps.action: For a non-matching roll, select an empty hand or another suitable Creative-mode slot, aim directly at the lectern, and break it with left-click. Ensure the lectern itself, rather than an enclosure block, is removed.
steps.success_cue: The lectern block is gone and the villager remains safely inside the enclosure.

steps.action: Wait until the untraded villager releases the destroyed lectern and visibly loses the librarian profession. Do not continue merely because the lectern has disappeared. If the villager remains a librarian, verify that no trade was completed and that there is no second lectern nearby, then continue waiting while the frozen daytime remains active.
steps.success_cue: The villager no longer wears the librarian outfit and is again unemployed.

steps.action: Select the Lectern again and right-click the same accessible floor position to replace it. Wait until the villager reclaims it and visibly becomes a librarian again; this generates a fresh set of unlocked trades.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the original lectern position with Lectern selected
steps.success_cue: The lectern is present, the villager has regained the librarian outfit, and the next trade inspection can begin.

steps.action: Repeat steps 16 through 21 as a controlled reroll loop. On each iteration, first open and inspect the fresh trades. If no Density, Breach, or Wind Burst Enchanted Book is offered, close the interface, break the lectern, wait for the profession to be lost, replace the lectern, and wait for the profession to return. On the first iteration where one of those book tooltips is visible, make no trade and stop immediately at step 17.
steps.exact_input: Repeat steps 16-21 until the tooltip inspected in step 17 is Density, Breach, or Wind Burst
steps.success_cue: The Trading screen for a freshly rerolled, untraded librarian remains open, with the pointer hovering over the selected Enchanted Book output and its tooltip visible.

stor.handoff_condition: On the matching reroll, the newly generated novice librarian Trading screen has just been opened and the cursor is hovering over the relevant Enchanted Book output so its tooltip is visible. The world still has no Update 1.21 or Villager Trade Rebalance experimental datapack enabled, and no trade with this villager has been completed. Begin observation without clicking, closing the screen, or changing the villager's workstation.
uncertainties: The report lists both 24w13a and 1.20.5 Release Candidate 1 as affected but does not identify a preferred test version. Release Candidate 1 is recommended because a report comment explicitly confirms reproduction there; 24w13a is an alternative affected version.

The report does not supply a seed, coordinates, game mode, world type, server requirement, or villager acquisition method. The single-player Creative Superflat setup is therefore a practical inference intended to remove unrelated exploration and resource gathering.
The unavailable image attachment may have shown a particular mace enchantment, level, villager tier, price, or interface arrangement. Those details cannot be preserved from the supplied text.
The report says to keep rerolling until a mace enchantment appears but gives no deterministic random seed, probability, or maximum attempt count. The number of loop iterations is therefore unbounded.

The report does not explicitly name the villager profession. A librarian is used because the reproduction concerns a villager offering an enchantment as an Enchanted Book and lectern replacement is the established way to reroll an untraded librarian's offers.

The report does not state whether all three mace-only enchantments demonstrated the issue. Density, Breach, and Wind Burst are all treated as matching targets because those are the three mace-specific enchantments introduced for the affected experimental feature set.

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.2 (explicitly listed as affected in the report)
stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.2 in a single-player Creative-mode world using the integrated server, with commands enabled. Perform the reproduction in the Overworld on flat, open ground with no roof above the target villager and no other villagers nearby. Use Normal difficulty. The instructions assume default keyboard and mouse controls; if controls are rebound, use the equivalent Open Chat, Use Item/Place Block, Jump/Fly, and Sneak/Descend actions.
preconditions: The launcher can start the exact Java Edition 1.21.2 installation rather than a later release or snapshot.
The test world permits commands and command-block use.
The player is in Creative mode so the pen and delayed command-block circuit can be built without gathering materials.
Use a new or otherwise controlled area with no other villagers in loaded chunks; the command block selects the nearest villager.
Keep the target pen and redstone circuit within the same normally loaded area.
Do not put a roof over the target pen.
The lever must remain off until the actual trigger sequence.

steps.action: Launch the exact affected Minecraft Java Edition installation from the launcher.
steps.success_cue: The main menu displays Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.2.

steps.action: Create a new single-player world. Set the game mode to Creative and enable commands before creating the world. A flat or Superflat world is preferred, but is not required.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Allow Commands: On -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: World generation begins with Creative mode and commands enabled.

steps.action: Wait for world loading to finish before entering commands or building anything.
steps.success_cue: Surrounding terrain is rendered, the player can move normally, and chat opens without loading delay.

steps.action: Press T to open chat, enter the difficulty command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the difficulty is Normal.

steps.action: Open chat, clear the weather to prevent unrelated natural lightning during setup, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The sky is clear and chat confirms the weather change.

steps.action: Open chat and disable the weather cycle so the controlled setup remains clear.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that doWeatherCycle is now false.

steps.action: Open chat and set the time to daytime so an unemployed villager can claim a workstation.
steps.success_cue: The world is visibly in daytime and chat confirms the time change.

steps.action: Open chat and freeze the daylight cycle while it is daytime.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that doDaylightCycle is now false and daylight remains stable.

steps.action: Move to a level outdoor workspace away from villages and other villagers. Leave at least 25 blocks of unobstructed ground in one direction for the repeater line.
steps.exact_input: W/A/S/D; double-tap Space to fly if necessary
steps.success_cue: There is enough flat space for a small villager pen and a straight 20-repeater line, with no other villagers visible nearby.

steps.action: Open chat and give yourself ten oak fences for the holding pen.
steps.success_cue: Ten oak fences are present in the player's inventory.

steps.action: Open chat and give yourself one lectern, which will be used as the villager's workstation.
steps.success_cue: A lectern is present in the player's inventory.

steps.action: Open chat and give yourself one lever for activating the delayed circuit.
steps.success_cue: A lever is present in the player's inventory.

steps.action: Open chat and give yourself twenty redstone repeaters.
steps.success_cue: Twenty redstone repeaters are present in the player's inventory.

steps.action: Open chat and give yourself one command block.
steps.success_cue: A command block is present in the player's inventory.

steps.action: Select the oak fences and place all ten as the perimeter of a 4-by-3-block rectangle. The completed perimeter must leave exactly two adjacent ground blocks as its 2-by-1 interior. Do not add a roof.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once for each fence placement
steps.success_cue: A closed fence pen with a two-block interior and open sky above it is complete.

steps.action: Select the lectern and place it on one of the two ground blocks inside the pen. Leave the other interior block empty for the villager.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the chosen interior ground block
steps.success_cue: The lectern occupies one interior cell and the adjacent interior cell remains empty.

steps.action: Use Creative flight to enter the empty interior cell without breaking the fence. Double-tap Space to start flying, move over the fence, and use Left Shift to descend into the empty cell.
steps.exact_input: Double-tap Space -> movement keys -> Left Shift
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the pen's empty interior cell directly beside the lectern.

steps.action: While standing in the empty interior cell, press T, summon a default adult villager at the player's current position using the exact command, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: An adult villager appears in the pen beside the lectern.

steps.action: Immediately use Creative flight to leave the pen without removing any fences or the lectern.
steps.exact_input: Double-tap Space -> movement keys -> Left Shift to land outside
steps.success_cue: The player is outside the closed pen while the villager and lectern remain inside.

steps.action: Wait for the villager to claim the lectern and become a librarian. Do not proceed while it still has the plain unemployed appearance.
steps.success_cue: Green job-site particles may appear, and the villager visibly wears the librarian profession outfit, confirming that its trading interface is available.

steps.action: Select the lever and place it on the ground immediately outside the fence, close enough that the player can activate it and then target the villager without walking more than a few blocks. Leave the lever in its initial off position.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the ground beside the pen
steps.success_cue: An unpowered lever is present beside the pen and the villager can be reached with the Use action from the same general position.

steps.action: Select the repeaters. Starting directly adjacent to the lever, place all twenty in one continuous straight line extending away from the pen. Each repeater must face away from the lever so its output leads toward the next repeater. Stand behind each placement and face down the intended signal direction when placing it.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once per repeater while facing away from the lever
steps.success_cue: A continuous line runs from the lever through exactly twenty repeaters, and every repeater points toward the far end of the line.

steps.action: Set every repeater to its maximum four-redstone-tick delay. Starting from the first repeater, right-click each repeater exactly three times without breaking or changing its orientation.
steps.exact_input: Right-click each of the 20 repeaters three times
steps.success_cue: The two small repeater torches on every repeater are at their maximum separation; twenty maximum-delay repeaters provide approximately eight seconds before the command block is powered.

steps.action: Select the command block and place it directly against the output side of the twentieth repeater so that the final repeater points into and powers the command block.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the ground immediately beyond repeater 20
steps.success_cue: The command block is directly adjacent to the last repeater at the output end of the line.

steps.action: Right-click the command block to open its configuration interface.
steps.success_cue: The command-block configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Enter the lightning command exactly as shown, without a leading slash. Keep the command block set to Impulse, Unconditional, and Needs Redstone, then click Done. The selector intentionally uses the nearest villager to the command block, so the target must be the only nearby villager.
steps.success_cue: The configuration screen closes, the command block remains unpowered, and its saved command will summon lightning at the nearest villager when the delayed signal arrives.

steps.action: Return to the lever beside the pen. Select an empty hotbar slot so no held item interferes when using the villager. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen; use the number key for an empty slot or the mouse wheel to select it.
steps.exact_input: Number key for an empty hotbar slot, or mouse wheel
steps.success_cue: The player's hand is empty, the lever is within reach, and the librarian can be targeted immediately afterward.

steps.action: Aim at the lever and activate the delayed command-block setup using the Use action. Do not activate it more than once.
steps.success_cue: The lever visibly switches to its on position and the first repeater begins the delayed signal sequence.

steps.action: Immediately turn toward the employed villager, aim directly at its exposed upper body or head over the fence, and use the villager before the delayed signal reaches the command block. The default Use action is right-click.
steps.success_cue: The villager trading interface is open, showing its trade offers, before the lightning command executes.

steps.action: Keep the trading interface open. Do not press Esc, the inventory key, or any control that closes the interface. Do not pause the game.
steps.success_cue: The trading interface remains the active screen while the delayed redstone signal continues toward the command block.

steps.action: Wait in the open trading interface until the twenty-repeaters delay finishes and the command block summons lightning at the targeted villager. Stop further player input as soon as the controlled lightning event occurs.
steps.success_cue: A lightning flash and thunder event has just occurred at the target villager while its trading interface was already open; the trigger has completed and observation should begin immediately.

stor.handoff_condition: The target librarian's trading interface was opened before the delayed command fired, and command-summoned lightning has just struck the target. Keep the current screen and player state unchanged and hand control to the observation subsystem immediately.
uncertainties: The report does not provide the original command-block command, circuit geometry, or delay length. This plan uses a deterministic nearest-villager execute command and twenty maximum-delay repeaters, producing approximately eight seconds to open the interface.
The report does not specify the villager profession. A lectern and librarian were selected as the simplest deterministic way to satisfy the stated requirement that the villager have a job.
No world seed, coordinates, or server requirement are supplied. The plan therefore uses a controlled single-player Creative world and an arbitrary clear workspace.
The attachment contents are not included in the supplied report, so their exact build arrangement cannot be preserved.
Villager workstation claiming can occasionally take a short time. The plan freezes the world during daytime and requires visible profession acquisition before the circuit is activated.

source_meta._title: Wandering traders can sell pale oak saplings even when they're disabled

stor.environment: A new, disposable singleplayer Java Edition 24w40a world using the integrated server. Use Creative mode with commands allowed. The Winter Drop experiment must remain disabled; no datapacks or mods are required.
preconditions: Configure a Minecraft Launcher installation to run the exact affected snapshot, 24w40a.
Use a newly created test world rather than upgrading an existing world, so its experiment settings are unambiguous.
Keep the Winter Drop experiment disabled while creating the world. For the most isolated setup, leave every experiment disabled.
Allow commands so wandering traders can be spawned and removed quickly without waiting for natural spawning.
The relevant trade is randomly selected. The report provides no seed, fixed attempt count, or deterministic trader data, so multiple freshly spawned traders may need to be sampled.
Do not inject a Pale Oak Sapling trade through entity NBT or commands; each trader must use its naturally randomized offers.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select or create an installation for the exact Java Edition snapshot 24w40a, then start the game with that installation.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and identifies the running version as 24w40a.

steps.action: From the main menu, open Singleplayer and select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: On the Game tab, set Game Mode to Creative. This avoids survival preparation and permits unrestricted interaction during repeated trials.
steps.success_cue: The world configuration displays Creative as the selected game mode.

steps.action: On the Game tab, set Allow Commands to On so the trader summon and cleanup commands can be executed from in-game chat.
steps.success_cue: The world configuration displays that commands are allowed.

steps.action: Open the experiment configuration from the world-creation screen by selecting More, then Experiments.
steps.success_cue: The Experiments screen is open and includes an entry named Winter Drop.

steps.action: Ensure the toggle beside Winter Drop is Off. Do not enable it. For an isolated test, also leave all other experiment toggles Off, then select Done to return to world creation.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen is restored without Winter Drop having been enabled.

steps.action: Select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The player enters the newly generated world.

steps.action: Wait until the surrounding terrain has rendered and player movement responds normally. Do not execute the test while the initial world-loading overlay or severe chunk-loading delay remains.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is visible, the loading overlay is gone, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Move to a reasonably flat, unobstructed location with at least two blocks of vertical clearance and free space within a few blocks of the player. Stop moving before summoning the trader.
steps.success_cue: There is a clear standing position near the player where a wandering trader can appear and be targeted.

steps.action: Press the default Open Chat key to open in-game chat.
steps.success_cue: The chat command input is active.

steps.action: Enter the wandering trader summon command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter. The relative coordinates place the trader two blocks toward positive Z from the player.
steps.success_cue: A new wandering trader is visible within a few blocks of the player, and the command does not report a syntax or permission error.

steps.action: Immediately aim the crosshair at the newly summoned wandering trader and press the Use Item/Place Block control once; with default mouse controls, this is right-click. Do not attack the trader and do not supply custom trade NBT.
steps.success_cue: The wandering trader trading interface is open and its list of randomized offers is available for the observation subsystem to inspect.

steps.action: If the observation subsystem reports that another randomized trader must be sampled, press Esc to close the current trading interface. Otherwise, leave the interface open and end the reproduction sequence.
steps.success_cue: When a retry is required, the trading interface is closed and normal world control has returned.

steps.action: For a requested retry, press T to open chat for cleanup.
steps.success_cue: The chat command input is active.

steps.action: Remove the nearest wandering trader so traders do not accumulate and obstruct targeting. Enter the cleanup command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The previously inspected wandering trader is no longer present, leaving the test area ready for a fresh randomized trader.

steps.action: Repeat steps 10 through 15 for freshly summoned wandering traders. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately after step 12 on every attempt; continue the loop only when that subsystem requests another sample.
steps.success_cue: Each trial opens the trade interface of one newly summoned trader, and rejected samples are removed before the next trial.

stor.handoff_condition: A newly summoned wandering trader's trading interface has just been opened in a 24w40a world created with Winter Drop disabled. The randomized offer list is visible and ready for the observation subsystem to inspect. If the observation subsystem requests another sample, resume at step 13.
uncertainties: The report does not state how many traders were required before the relevant randomized offer appeared; no maximum attempt count is supported by the report.
The report does not specify a game mode or whether spawn eggs or commands were used. Creative mode with the summon command is a practical choice supported by the report's permitted command method.
The report supplies no world seed, coordinates, or trader NBT that deterministically selects the relevant offer. Random offer sampling must therefore be preserved.
Leaving every experiment disabled is an isolation choice; the report strictly requires only that Winter Drop be disabled.
